MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 21, 2026

1.  CALL TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR NICKLAS at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR NICKLAS led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Nicklas, Romanelli, Medawar, Olson, Schachter, Yoo

Commissioners Absent:  Repp-Loadsman

City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Dev/Public Works Director
  Robert Khuu, Assistant City Attorney
  Katrina Kawagoe, Senior Planner
  Carol Corea, Interim Administrative Assistant

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, AUGUST 3, 2026

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  YOO to:

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 3, 2026.

There being no objection, CHAIR NICKLAS ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  CHAIR NICKLAS made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR NICKLAS so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-260298; ADDRESS: 3B Peninsula Center,
  Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Pierre Derbier, Alain Yotnegparian
  Architects; DESCRIPTION: A request for approval of a Precise Plan of Design (PPD-
  1
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 21, 2026
   260299) for minor exterior modifications, limited to the installation of a new sliding
  door, along with the interior remodel of an existing commercial building located within
  the Peninsula Shopping Center.

Senior Planner Kawagoe presented Planning Application No. PA-260298. In June 2026, staff
ministerially approved interior tenant improvements for a 2,790 square foot Canaan Chinese
Restaurant, a restaurant and bar. During the building plan check process, exterior
modifications were added to the plans which were not approved by Planning. Exterior
improvements to commercial properties require discretionary review; therefore, the applicant
has submitted a Precise Plan of Design application to bring the exterior improvements into
compliance. The applicant’s proposal includes a restaurant and full bar with indoor and
outdoor seating. The restaurant is a permitted use in the CGMU district, and alcohol is
permitted under Resolution No. 2318, a master conditional use permit for the Peninsula
Shopping Center. The proposal also includes the installation of a 14-foot sliding glass door
between the restaurant and the outdoor seating area. The existing patio perimeter fence has
been modified with a new access gate and secondary door. The storefront modification does
not impact the structure of the building.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that the project meets the requirement of the Precise Plan
of Design (PPD) criteria and staff can support the PPD as proposed. She stated that notices
were mailed to a 500’ radius from the subject property on September 10, 2026, and staff did
not receive any correspondence.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that in preparation for this meeting, staff went to the site to
take additional photos and found that additional modifications were made to the exterior of
the building that were not included in the plans. Staff contacted property management and
were informed that the full scope of work was not disclosed to them and therefore not
approved.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommend an additional condition of approval as
follows:

  “The unpermitted outdoor seating are structure/patio cover will be completely
  removed prior to final inspection and issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy”.

Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that in accordance with the California Environmental Quality
Act and the State CEQA guidelines, the project was determined to be categorically exempt
under Clase 1 Section 15301 existing facilities and staff recommends that the Planning
Commission approve Planning Application No. 260298, subject to the conditions outline in
the staff report, and the recommended condition of approval related to the unpermitted patio
structure.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked for clarification on the unpermitted structure. Senior
Planner Kawagoe clarified that it is the enclosed patio structure on the exterior of the building
and it is not approved and was not included in the plan set included with the staff report.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if staff recommended that the structure is removed
prior to issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy. Senior Planner Kawagoe responded, yes.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there was an explanation of why the structure was
built without permits. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that there was confusion about what
had allowed during the plan check process.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the purpose of the enclosed structure. Senior
Planner Kawagoe stated that she believes it is a shade structure; the moveable louvres allow
light in, and the shades also come up.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there were any circumstances where Vestar (property
management) would approve the structure. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that it would not
be approved as it is currently presented.

  2
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 21, 2026
 Charlie Candelas, Consultant for Ownership, stated that there may be some
miscommunication and stated that they do have approval for the structure from Vestar. Mr.
Candelas clarified that in between the columns of the structure there are screens; it is a free-
standing structure and is not attached to the building as required by Vestar. The purpose of
this structure is to provide additional seating to meet the income level requirements. The
structure provides a more comfortable and appealing space for patrons, and the sliding glass
system provides a seamless transition from the restaurant to the patio area.

CHAIR NICKLAS asked for clarification on the approval by Vestar. Mr. Candelas stated that
plans with the structure were submitted and approved by Vestar.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI asked if the applicant has plans signed by Vestar. Joshua Kot,
Canaan Restaurant Representative, explained that he has been in communication with
Vestar Corporate in Arizona who approved the overall concept, but are waiting for structural
plans and calculations. Mr. Kot stated that he believes that this is where there was a
breakdown in communication, and the contractor assumed the structure was approved. Mr.
Kot explained that there was confusion on what had been approved by building and safety
and they realized later that planning had not approved the project.

CHAIR NICKLAS stated that it sounds as though the sliding glass system was approved and
the enclosed patio structure was not approved. Mr. Kot stated that the sliding glass system
and the enclosed patio structure were submitted as one package to Vestar.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER suggested continuing this item to the next Planning
Commission meeting of October 5. Director Naughton stated that the structure was not
included in the plans that were submitted to building and safety and staff confirmed with
Vestar that they did not approve the structure. Mr. Kot agreed and asked if the structure can
remain until the next meeting.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked staff to confirm that the structure was not included in
the plan set submitted with the staff report. Senior Planner Kawagoe confirmed that the
structure was not shown on the plans; the plans only show the outline of the patio.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if staff would have any objection to the proposed
structure. Senior Planner Kawagoe stated that staff would need to further review the plans
for the structure. Director Naughton added that building and safety would need to review the
structure for ADA accessibility. Mr. Kot added that the structure is within the existing patio
outline.

COMMISSION OLSON asked if there are any safety concerns with the proximity of the
parking area to the enclosed structure.

Director Naughton clarified if the safety concern question was related to the screens as
opposed to having metal railings around the patio area which would act as a barrier and
COMMISSIONER OLSON confirmed. Mr. Candelas stated that there is additional metal in
the patio structure compared to the previous railing.

In response to a question from VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI, Senior Planner Kawagoe stated
that the project was approved by planning for a tenant improvement; as the project went
through building plan check the sliding glass system was approved without planning
approval. Director Naughton stated that the enclosed structure was not reviewed nor
approved by building and safety.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that the two items to be reviewed at the next meeting are
1) the plan submittal after the fact; 2) the unpermitted exterior enclosed patio cover.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  CONTINUE ITEM NO. PA-260298 TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING SCHEDULED FOR OCTOBER 5, 2026.

  AYES:  Nicklas, Romanelli, Medawar, Olson, Schachter, Yoo
  3
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 21, 2026
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Repp-Loadsman
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-260149; ADDRESS: 6 Encanto Drive, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Costa Gurevitch; DESCRIPTION: A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-260199) for a 626 SF pool and spa
  located within the front yard and Variances for the construction of a structure within the
  front yard setback (V-260200), to exceed the allowable overall lot coverage (V-260201),
  to exceed the allowable front yard lot coverage (V-260202), and for a fence/hedge
  exceeding two feet in height located in the front yard (V-260270).

Director Naughton presented Planning Application No. PA-260149. The subject property is
zoned RA-20, is not located within the Horse Overlay Zone, and is within the Montecillo HOA.
Property owners within a 500-foot radius were notified of the proposed project, and staff
received no comment letters. The 16,353-square-foot property is triangular in shape and
features an east-to-west downward slope. Due to the irregular configuration of the lot, the
existing residence was constructed with two legal nonconforming setbacks: a 10-foot rear-yard
setback and a 21.5-foot front-yard setback. In 1998, the Planning Commission approved
Resolution No. PA-10-98, granting a Variance to maintain the two legal nonconforming
setbacks and a Minor Deviation to reduce the required front-yard area by 10%. The approvals
facilitated demolition of the detached garage and construction of a 1,600-square-foot addition
and a 400-square-foot attached garage. The applicant is proposing to construct a new 626-
square-foot swimming pool and spa within the front-yard setback at the northeast corner of the
property. The Building and Safety Department would require a 5-foot-high fence around the
perimeter of the pool and spa. The proposal also includes a 6-foot hedge along Encanto Drive
to provide additional screening.

The pool mechanical equipment would be located at the southeast corner of the property within
a 5-foot-high wooden enclosure, as required by the City’s Municipal Code.

The proposed improvements would result in an increase in front-yard and overall lot coverage
beyond the maximum permitted in the RA-20 zoning district.

Director Naughton stated that staff have determined that the project conforms with the
Neighborhood Compatibility ordinance and provided findings to support the four Variances
requested.

Director Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public
hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues, close the public hearing; and adopt
Resolution No. PA-260149, approving the project.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the Planning Commission has approved a fence over two feet
in the front yard that did not include a pool. Director Naughton stated that the exception has
been for a 42-inch high three rail fence within the horse overlay district, any other fencing above
two feet would require a Variance.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR NICKLAS so ordered.

Evgeniya Ryabchikova, Property Owner, stated that she and her husband, Makoto Okuwa,
recently moved to the City and value the beauty and peaceful character of the community. She
stated that they view the property as their long-term family home and seek to improve it
thoughtfully and respectfully. She explained that the proposed pool and spa were designed to
accommodate the unique configuration and physical characteristics of the lot, requiring several
Variances. She emphasized that the Variances are necessary for a functional and well-
  4
Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 21, 2026
 designed project, rather than to maximize development or convenience. She stated that they
have made efforts to minimize impacts on neighboring properties. She stated that the pool is
intended for normal family use and to provide a safe, attractive space while remaining respectful
neighbors and responsible members of the community.

VICE CHAIR ROMANELLI asked if there was consideration to design the pool in a way that
would conform with the City’s municipal code. Mark Stone, on behalf of Property Owner Makoto
Okuwa, stated that the lot is a non-traditional shape and there is no room in the side or rear
yard to accommodate a pool. Mrs. Ryabchikova stated that shrubs will be replanted in that area.

CHAIR NICKLAS asked if the construction was going to take place from Encanto and inquired
about the need to cut down the shrubs to provide access.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR NICKLAS so ordered.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-260149, APPROVING THE PROJECT.

  AYES:  Nicklas, Medawar, Olson, Schachter, Yoo
  NOES:  Romanelli
  ABSENT:  Repp-Loadsman
  ABSTAIN:  None

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR reported that he has received complaints about trailers parked

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR reported that he has received a complaint about a property on

Director Naughton introduced Assistant City Attorney Robert Khuu to the Planning
